definition_zh: 充分地；足够地；合乎要求地
definition_en: in a way that is enough in amount, or good enough in quality, for a particular purpose
core_image: 往杯子里倒水，水面刚好停在杯壁那一道刻度线上
scene: 帐篷外的雨越下越大，队长挨个检查每个人的背包。The team was adequately equipped for the storm.
sceneCN: 这里的 adequately 是「充分地」（第 1 个义项：数量或程度上足够）；句意是队伍为这场暴风雨做了充分的装备。

pos.zh: 副词：充分地；足够地；合乎要求地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 还原为形容词，义为「足够的；适当的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「足够；适当」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不足的；不够格的」
由否定形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「不足；缺陷」

senses.title: Enough in amount
senses.definition: in a quantity or degree large enough to meet a need
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上大到足以满足需要
senses.example: The shelter was adequately stocked with food and water.
senses.exampleCN: 避难所储备了足够的食物和水。
senses.why: adequately is the adverb of adequate, which Latin built from adaequare, to make equal: the supply is made equal to the need.
senses.whyCN: adequately 是 adequate 的副词；拉丁语 adaequare 意为「使相等」，即把供给做到与需要相等。

senses.title: Good enough in quality
senses.definition: to a standard that is acceptable, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 达到可以接受的标准，但算不上出色
senses.example: She answered every question adequately, though without much flair.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个问题都答得合格，只是没什么出彩之处。
senses.why: Once the measure matches the demand, the result only has to cross the line, so the adverb often means acceptable rather than excellent.
senses.whyCN: 只要分量与需求相称，结果就只需过线，所以这个副词常表示「合格」而非「出色」。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of equality, turned into an adverb of sufficiency.
intro.cn: 一个来自拉丁语的「相等」形容词，变成了表示「足够」的副词。

items.en: aequus meant level, even or equal, and gave aequitas, fairness.
items.cn: aequus 意为平的、均匀的、相等的，并生出 aequitas「公平」。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus aequare 'to make equal' formed adaequare, to make equal to, to level up.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 aequare（使相等）构成 adaequare，意为「使与……相等、拉平」。

items.en: The participle adaequatus described a thing made proportionate to its measure.
items.cn: 分词 adaequatus 描述的是「被做得与其尺度相称」的事物。

items.en: English borrowed adequate from Latin in the seventeenth century; the adverb adequately followed it.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪直接从拉丁语借入 adequate，副词 adequately 随后出现。

items.en: Modern usage marks the line between enough and not enough, and often hints at 'only just enough'.
items.cn: 现代用法划出「够」与「不够」的分界，还常暗示「刚刚够」。

note.en: The first group shares the equality root; the second gathers adverbs of sufficiency with different shades.
note.cn: 第一组共享「相等」词根；第二组是几个表示「足够」的副词，语气各有差别。

entries.definition: the state of not being enough
to a degree that is enough
in a way that fits the purpose
to a fair but not high degree

normalIntro.en: Three pieces carry the word: ad-, aequus and -ly.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由三块拼成：ad-、aequus 与 -ly。

normal.en: ad- means to, aequus means equal, so adequately means up to the mark.
normal.cn: ad- 表示「向」，aequus 表示「相等」，adequately 就是「达到刻度」。

normal.en: The adjective ends in -ate and the adverb simply adds -ly.
normal.cn: 形容词以 -ate 结尾，副词直接加 -ly。

normal.en: adequately prepared is the commonest pairing in writing.
normal.cn: adequately prepared（准备充分）是书面语里最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Reports like to pair adequately funded with adequately staffed.
normal.cn: 报告里常把 adequately funded 与 adequately staffed 成对使用。

normal.en: Spell it with a single d in the middle: adequate.
normal.cn: 拼写中间只有一个 d：adequate。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler against a cup and the water stopping exactly at the line.
abstract.cn: 想象把尺子贴在杯壁上，水面刚好停在刻度线。

abstract.en: See a scale with the goods on one side and the need on the other, level.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端，一边是货物，一边是需要，正好持平。

abstract.en: Imagine a report card with every box ticked but no stars.
abstract.cn: 想象一张成绩单，每一栏都打了勾，却没有星。

examples.en: The shelter was adequately stocked with food and water.
examples.cn: 避难所储备了足够的食物和水。

examples.en: He was adequately paid for the extra hours.
examples.cn: 他加班的那几个小时得到了足够的报酬。

examples.en: The report adequately explains why the project failed.
examples.cn: 这份报告充分解释了项目失败的原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱得夸特利」——他爱夸自己准备得够充分，其实只是刚刚够用。

root: 拉丁语 adaequare（使相等），由 ad-（向）与 aequus（相等的）构成；adequate 本义是「与需要相称的」，加 -ly 成为副词。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb of measurement covers both quantity and quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表示「量」的副词，既管数量，也管质量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water stopping exactly at the marked line.
core.cn: 核心意象：水面正好停在刻度线上。

intro.cn: 一个表示方向的词头、一个表示相等的词根、一个副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: aequus also gives equilibrium and equator.
latinIntro.cn: aequus 也给出 equilibrium 与 equator。

definition_zh: 黏附；坚持；遵守；追随
definition_en: to stick firmly to a surface, or to hold firmly to a belief, rule or person
core_image: 一张标签牢牢贴在玻璃上，撕下来还留着一圈印子
scene: 墙上那块瓷砖已经松了，另一半海报却还紧紧贴着墙面。The old poster still adheres to the damp wall.
sceneCN: 这里的 adheres 是「黏附」（第 1 个义项：紧贴表面）；句意是那张旧海报仍然黏在潮湿的墙上。

pos.zh: 动词：黏附；坚持；遵守；追随

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「遵守；坚持；黏附」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「拥护者；黏附物」
由拉丁词干加名词后缀构成，义为「黏附；附着力」
由拉丁词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「黏性的；胶粘剂」

senses.title: To stick fast to a surface
senses.definition: to stick or hold firmly to a surface, often by natural or chemical means
senses.definitionCN: 紧紧贴住或附着在某个表面上，多靠自然力或化学作用
senses.example: The label adheres best to a dry, clean surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这种标签在干燥洁净的表面上黏得最牢。
senses.why: The Latin verb haerere means to stick or stay fixed, and ad- adds direction towards something, so the word pictures contact that will not let go.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 haerere 意为「粘住、固定不动」，ad- 又加上「朝向」的方向，所以这个词画出的是一种不肯松开的接触。

senses.title: To follow a rule or promise
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a rule, agreement or standard
senses.definitionCN: 按照规则、约定或标准行事
senses.example: All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工都必须遵守安全规定。
senses.why: A rule that you adhere to is one you stay stuck to; the physical image of clinging is transferred to conduct.
senses.whyCN: 你 adhere to 的规则，是你「贴住不放」的规则；身体上的黏附被移用到行为上。

senses.title: To stay loyal to a leader or group
senses.definition: to give continued support to a person, party or cause
senses.definitionCN: 持续支持某个人、政党或事业
senses.example: Several senators refused to adhere to the new party line.
senses.exampleCN: 几位参议员拒绝追随新的党派路线。
senses.why: Here people are the surfaces: supporters stay attached to a leader instead of drifting away.
senses.whyCN: 这里的人是「表面」：拥护者紧贴着领袖，而不是飘走。

intro.en: One Latin verb of sticking supplies both the physical and the moral senses.
intro.cn: 一个表示「粘住」的拉丁动词，同时供给了物理义与道义义。

items.en: haerere meant to stick, cling or stay fixed, and also to be stuck in doubt.
items.cn: haerere 意为粘住、紧贴、固定不动，也有「困在疑惑中」的意思。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus haerere formed adhaerere, to stick to, with the noun adhaesio for the act of sticking.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 haerere 构成 adhaerere「黏附于」，名词 adhaesio 表示黏附这一动作。

items.en: Old French adherer carried the physical and the figurative senses side by side.
items.cn: 古法语 adherer 把物理义与比喻义一并带了过来。

items.en: English took the verb in the fifteenth century, first for physical sticking, soon for holding to opinions.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，先指物理上的黏附，很快也指坚持某种意见。

items.en: Technical writing keeps the literal sense, while law and politics use it for obedience and loyalty.
items.cn: 技术文献保留字面义，法律与政治则用它表示遵守与忠诚。

note.en: The first group is the haerere family; the second gathers verbs of sticking and of compliance.
note.cn: 第一组是 haerere 词族；第二组收黏住与服从两路动词。

abstract.cn: 想象攀岩者的手死死扣住岩点。

abstract.en: Think of a member who never misses the party line.

sensesIntro.cn: 「粘住」这一个意象，同时管着胶水、规则与忠诚。

definition_zh: 毗连的；邻近的；紧接着的；（几何）邻接的
definition_en: next to or very near something, or immediately following it
core_image: 两栋房子共用同一面墙，门牌号只差一号
scene: 旅馆走廊尽头那扇门后，就是我们要找的房间。Our room is adjacent to the lecture hall.
sceneCN: 这里的 adjacent 是「毗连的」（第 1 个义项：位置紧挨着）；句意是我们的房间紧挨着报告厅。

pos.zh: 形容词：毗连的；邻近的；紧接着的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「邻接；邻近」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「相邻地」

senses.title: Next to in space
senses.definition: lying next to something or sharing a border with it
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物旁边，或与它共有一条边界
senses.example: The library is adjacent to the main gate.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆紧挨着正门。
senses.why: Latin adiacere is ad- 'near' plus iacere 'to lie', so the word literally pictures one thing lying beside another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adiacere 是 ad-（靠近）加 iacere（躺），字面就是「一物躺在另一物旁边」。

senses.title: Immediately following in order
senses.definition: coming immediately after something in a series, text or process
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列事物、文本或过程中紧接在某物之后
senses.example: The chapter adjacent to this one deals with grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 紧接这一章的那一章讲的是语法。
senses.why: If two things lie side by side on a page or in a list, the second one touches the first; nearness in space becomes nearness in order.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西在纸面或清单上并排躺着，后者就贴着前者；空间上的邻近于是变成顺序上的紧接。

senses.title: Sharing a side or vertex in geometry
senses.definition: describing angles or sides that share a common vertex or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 指角或边共用同一个顶点或边界
senses.example: In the figure, the two adjacent angles add up to a straight angle.
senses.exampleCN: 在图中，这两个邻角相加等于一个平角。
senses.why: Geometry keeps the oldest literal sense: two figures lie against each other along a shared edge.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留了最早的字面义：两个图形沿着一条共用的边彼此贴靠。

intro.en: A Latin verb of lying near became an adjective of nearness.
intro.cn: 一个表示「躺在旁边」的拉丁动词，变成了表示邻近的形容词。

items.en: iacere meant to lie down or to throw, and it underlies project and reject as well.
items.cn: iacere 意为躺下或投掷，project 与 reject 也出自这个词。

items.en: ad- 'near' plus iacere formed adiacere, to lie near, with the participle adiacens.
items.cn: ad-（靠近）加 iacere 构成 adiacere「位于附近」，分词为 adiacens。

items.en: The noun adiacentia named neighbourhood, the state of lying next to something.
items.cn: 名词 adiacentia 表示「邻近」，即紧挨着某物的状态。

items.en: English borrowed adjacent in the sixteenth century, mainly in geometry and land surveying.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 adjacent，主要用于几何与土地测量。

items.en: It now covers rooms, plots, fields and stages of a process, always stressing contact or nearness.
items.cn: 如今它可用于房间、地块、田野与流程阶段，始终强调接触或接近。

note.en: The first group shares the lying-near root; the second gathers words for being next to something.
note.cn: 第一组共享「躺在旁边」的词根；第二组是几个表示「紧挨」的词。

definition_zh: 调整；调节；适应；校准
definition_en: to change something slightly so that it fits, works or feels right
core_image: 司机扳动座椅旁的小手柄，椅背缓缓后仰到刚好的角度
scene: 水温太烫，她先放掉一些热水，又添了半杯凉的。She adjusted the shower before stepping in.
sceneCN: 这里的 adjusted 是「调节」（第 1 个义项：稍作改变以适合需要）；句意是她进浴室前先调好了水温。

pos.zh: 动词：调整；调节；适应；校准

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「调整；适应」
由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「可调节的」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「调节器；理算员」

senses.title: To change something slightly to fit
senses.definition: to change a thing a little so that it works better or fits a need
senses.definitionCN: 把某物稍作改变，使它运转得更好或更合需要
senses.example: Please adjust the mirror before you drive.
senses.exampleCN: 开车前请先调好后视镜。
senses.why: Old French ajuster meant to put right, from juste, exact; adjusting is bringing a thing to its exact point.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 ajuster 意为「摆正」，出自 juste（准确的）；adjust 就是把东西放到那个准确的点上。

senses.title: To get used to a new situation
senses.definition: to become used to new conditions, often gradually
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐习惯新的条件或环境
senses.example: It took her a month to adjust to the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个月才适应夜班。
senses.why: People also need setting right: the word moves from machines to the way a person's habits settle into a new place.
senses.whyCN: 人也需要「调正」：这个词从机器移用到一个人的习惯在新环境里安顿下来的过程。

senses.title: To set an instrument to a true value
senses.definition: to set a device or scale so that it measures accurately
senses.definitionCN: 把装置或刻度调到能准确测量的状态
senses.example: The technician adjusted the scale to zero.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员把秤校准到零点。
senses.why: Scientific use sharpens the idea of exactness: the instrument is brought back to the true mark.
senses.whyCN: 科学用法把「准确」这一层磨得更利：仪器被带回真正的刻度上。

intro.en: A French word of exactness, rooted in Latin ideas of near and just.
intro.cn: 一个来自法语的「准确」之词，根子扎在拉丁语的「邻近」与「正当」里。

items.en: iuxta was an adverb meaning near, close by, and it survives in juxtapose.
items.cn: iuxta 是副词，意为「在近旁」，juxtapose 里还留着它。

items.en: iustus meant just or exact, and gave justice and justify.
items.cn: iustus 意为正当的、准确的，生出 justice 与 justify。

items.en: ajuster meant to put right or arrange, built from a- 'to' plus juste 'exact'.
items.cn: ajuster 意为「摆正、安排」，由 a-（向）加 juste（准确）构成。

items.en: English borrowed adjust in the seventeenth century, at first meaning to arrange or settle a matter.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 adjust，最初表示「安排、了结一件事」。

items.en: Instruments gave it the sense of setting a scale; psychology added people adjusting to change.
items.cn: 仪器赋予它「校准刻度」之义；心理学又添上「人适应变化」这一层。

note.en: The first group is the adjust family; the second gathers verbs of fitting and setting.
note.cn: 第一组是 adjust 词族；第二组收「使适合」与「设定」两路动词。

entries.definition: a small change made to fit
able to be changed to fit
a person or device that adjusts
to change to suit new conditions
to set an instrument to the right pitch
to mark or set an instrument accurately

normalIntro.en: The word came through French from Latin iuxta, near.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词经由法语来自拉丁语 iuxta，意为「靠近」。

normal.en: adjust carries the idea of bringing something to the just point.
normal.cn: adjust 的核心是把东西带到「刚好」的那个点上。

normal.en: adjust to is the pattern for people getting used to change.
normal.cn: adjust to 是人适应变化的固定搭配。

normal.en: adjustment is the noun and adjustable the adjective.
normal.cn: adjustment 是名词，adjustable 是形容词。

normal.en: adjust the volume and adjust the seat are everyday phrases.
normal.cn: adjust the volume 与 adjust the seat 是日常搭配。

normal.en: Keep the double d: adjust, not ajust.
normal.cn: 记住双 d：是 adjust，不是 ajust。

abstract.en: See a dial turned a fraction until the sound is right.
abstract.cn: 想象旋钮只转了一点点，声音就刚好了。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller shifting sleep hours after a long flight.
abstract.cn: 想象长途飞行后，旅人一点点挪动作息。

abstract.en: Think of a scale needle settling on zero.
abstract.cn: 想象秤针慢慢停在零位。

examples.en: Please adjust the mirror before you drive.
examples.cn: 开车前请先调好后视镜。

examples.en: It took her a month to adjust to the night shift.
examples.cn: 她花了一个月才适应夜班。

examples.en: The technician adjusted the scale to zero.
examples.cn: 技术员把秤校准到零点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿得贾斯特」——饿得发慌的贾斯特，先把椅子调到最舒服的角度再坐下。

root: 古法语 ajuster（摆正），源自拉丁语 iuxta（靠近）与 iustus（准确）；本义是「使恰到好处」，后分化为调节、适应与校准。

sensesIntro.en: Setting a thing right covers machines, habits and instruments.
sensesIntro.cn: 把东西「调正」这一动作，管着机器、习惯与仪器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial turned a hair until it clicks into place.
core.cn: 核心意象：旋钮微微一转，咔地到位。

branches.en: a driver sliding the seat back
a newcomer settling into a new job
a needle set back to zero
bringing a thing to its true value
branches.cn: 把事物带到它的真值上

branches.en: the body adapting to thin air

intro.en: A French verb of setting right, with Latin roots of near and just.
intro.cn: 一个表示「摆正」的法语动词，根子连着拉丁语的「近」与「准」。

latinIntro.en: iuxta also appears in juxtapose and juxtaposition.
latinIntro.cn: iuxta 也出现在 juxtapose 与 juxtaposition 里。

definition_zh: 管理；实施；给予（药物、援助）；主持
definition_en: to manage an organization or system, to put something into effect, or to give a drug or help to someone
core_image: 一只手在账本上落下最后一行，另一只手把药片递到病人掌心
scene: 医院人手不够，院长亲自排班，又去库房清点物资。The director administers the hospital's small budget herself.
sceneCN: 这里的 administers 是「管理」（第 1 个义项：掌管日常事务）；句意是院长亲自管理医院那笔不多的预算。

pos.zh: 动词：管理；实施；给予；主持

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「管理；行政部门」
由动词词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「行政的；管理的」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由名词逆构而成的动词，义为「管理；执行」

senses.title: To manage the running of an organization
senses.definition: to be in charge of the daily work, money or affairs of an institution
senses.definitionCN: 负责某个机构的日常工作、资金或事务
senses.example: She administers a team of forty nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 她管理着一支四十人的护士队伍。
senses.why: Latin minister meant a servant, and administrare meant to serve or manage affairs for someone, so the word still carries the idea of handling business on another's behalf.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 minister 指仆人，administrare 意为「为他人服务、替人理事」，所以这个词至今带着「代他人打理事务」的意思。

senses.title: To give a drug or treatment
senses.definition: to give a medicine, treatment or form of help to a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 把药物、治疗或帮助给予人或动物
senses.example: Nurses administer the vaccine at the school clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在学校医务室接种疫苗。
senses.why: Serving someone came to include handing them what they need; medicine fixed the pattern as administer a drug.
senses.whyCN: 「服务他人」这一层引申出「把所需之物递到对方手上」，医学把这个搭配固定为 administer a drug。

senses.title: To put law or justice into effect
senses.definition: to carry out a law, a system or a form of justice in practice
senses.definitionCN: 在实际中执行法律、制度或某种公正
senses.example: The court administers justice without favour.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭执法不偏不倚。
senses.why: Managing affairs includes running the machinery of law, so the word came to name the act of making justice operate.
senses.whyCN: 管理事务也包括让法律机器运转，于是这个词被用来指「让公正真正生效」的动作。

senses.title: To lead a formal ceremony
senses.definition: to conduct a formal act such as an oath or a sacrament
senses.definitionCN: 主持宣誓、圣礼等正式仪式
senses.example: The judge administered the oath to the new citizens.
senses.exampleCN: 法官主持了新公民的宣誓仪式。
senses.why: A ceremony is also an affair to be managed; the one who serves it along is the one who administers it.
senses.whyCN: 仪式同样是一件需要料理的事务；把它一步步走完的人，就是在 administer 它。

intro.en: A Latin verb of serving grew into the vocabulary of management.
intro.cn: 一个表示「服务」的拉丁动词，长成了管理领域的词汇。

items.en: minister meant a servant or attendant, one who waits on another.
items.cn: minister 指仆人、随从，即服侍他人的人。

items.en: ministrare meant to serve, to wait on, and later to supply or furnish.
items.cn: ministrare 意为服侍、伺候，后来也指供给、提供。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus ministrare formed administrare, to serve, to manage affairs for someone.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 ministrare 构成 administrare，意为「服务、替人管理事务」。

items.en: Old French administrer narrowed the sense towards managing business or property.
items.cn: 古法语 administrer 把词义收窄到管理事务或财产。

items.en: English took the verb in the fifteenth century, first for managing affairs, later for giving medicine and law.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入该动词，先指管理事务，后来才用于给药与执法。

note.en: The first group is the minister family; the second gathers verbs of running, giving and enforcing.
note.cn: 第一组是 minister 词族；第二组收「管理」「给予」「执行」三类动词。

entries.definition: the work of managing an institution
to be in charge of something
to give out medicine or supplies
to make people obey a law

normalIntro.en: Inside the word sits minister, a servant.
normalIntro.cn: 词里藏着 minister，也就是「仆人」。

normal.en: administrare meant to serve, so to administer is to take care of affairs for others.
normal.cn: administrare 意为服务，所以 administer 是替别人照料事务。

normal.en: The same stem yields administration, administrator and administrative.
normal.cn: 同一词干生出 administration、administrator 与 administrative。

normal.en: Medicine fixed the phrase administer a drug.
normal.cn: 医学固定了 administer a drug（给药）这一说法。

normal.en: Law fixed the phrase administer justice.
normal.cn: 法律固定了 administer justice（执法）这一说法。

normal.en: Note the -ister ending, as in minister and register.
normal.cn: 注意词尾是 -ister，与 minister、register 相同。

abstract.en: See a steward carrying accounts in one hand and a tray in the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一位管家一手拿账本，一手端托盘。

abstract.en: Picture a nurse checking a dose twice before handing it over.
abstract.cn: 想象护士把剂量核对两遍才递出去。

abstract.en: Think of a judge making the law actually work in a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象法官让法律在法庭里真正运转起来。

examples.en: Nurses administer the vaccine at the school clinic.
examples.cn: 护士在学校医务室接种疫苗。

examples.en: The court administers justice without favour.
examples.cn: 法庭执法不偏不倚。

examples.en: He administered the fund for twenty years.
examples.cn: 他管理这笔基金二十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的米尼斯特」——额头上写着米尼斯特的名字，因为他是替大家管事的管家。

root: 拉丁语 administrare（服务、理事），由 ad-（向）与 ministrare（服侍）构成，词根 minister 意为「仆人」；本义「替人打理事务」，后引申为给药与执法。

sensesIntro.en: One verb of serving covers budgets, medicines, courts and ceremonies.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「服务」动词，管着预算、药物、法庭与仪式。

core.cn: 核心意象：管家替他人料理事务。

branches.cn: 护士把药递到病人手上

a judge leading an oath
handing over what the rule or the body requires
branches.cn: 把规则或身体所需之物交付出去

intro.cn: 一个表示方向的词头，加一个表示「服侍」的词根。

latinIntro.en: minister also gives ministry and ministerial.
latinIntro.cn: minister 还生出 ministry 与 ministerial。

definition_zh: 管理；行政部门；政府；施用
definition_en: the work of managing an organization, the people who manage it, or the act of giving a drug
core_image: 一栋办公楼里，文件在各部门之间来回传递
scene: 新学期的课表迟迟没有下来，学生们结伴去办公室询问。The administration promised a new timetable by Friday.
sceneCN: 这里的 administration 是「行政部门」（第 2 个义项：负责管理的机构与人）；句意是行政部门承诺周五前给出新课表。

pos.zh: 名词：管理；行政部门；政府；施用

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「管理；施行」
由名词词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「行政的」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「管理者」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「在行政上」

senses.title: The work of managing an institution
senses.definition: the activity of organizing and running the affairs of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 组织并处理某个机构各项事务的活动
senses.example: Good administration keeps a school running smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的管理让学校运转顺畅。
senses.why: The noun names the activity behind administrare, the Latin verb for managing affairs for someone else.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指的就是拉丁动词 administrare（替人理事）背后的那项活动。

senses.title: The body of people who manage
senses.definition: the group of officials and staff who run an institution
senses.definitionCN: 负责运营某个机构的官员与职员群体
senses.example: The hospital administration approved the new rota.
senses.exampleCN: 医院管理层批准了新的排班表。
senses.why: The activity is easily replaced by the people who perform it, a common shift from action to agent.
senses.whyCN: 「活动」很容易转指「做这件事的人」，这是从行为到施动者的常见转喻。

senses.title: A government in office
senses.definition: the government of a country, especially in American usage
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家的政府，尤用于美式英语
senses.example: The administration cut taxes in its first year.
senses.exampleCN: 这届政府在上任第一年减了税。
senses.why: Running a state is the largest case of managing affairs, so the word stands for the whole governing team.
senses.whyCN: 治理国家是「管理事务」的最大一例，于是这个词直接指整个执政团队。

senses.title: The giving of a drug
senses.definition: the act of giving a medicine or treatment to a patient
senses.definitionCN: 把药物或治疗给予病人的行为
senses.example: The nurse recorded the administration of the drug.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录了这次给药。
senses.why: Medical writing borrowed the noun to label the moment when a dose is handed over.
senses.whyCN: 医学写作借来这个名词，用来标记「一剂药被交到病人手上」的那一刻。

intro.en: The noun of managing, built on the Latin verb of serving.
intro.cn: 表示「管理」的名词，建立在拉丁语「服侍」动词之上。

items.en: ministrare meant to serve or supply, from minister, a servant.
items.cn: ministrare 意为服侍或供给，出自 minister（仆人）。

items.en: administratio named the handling or management of affairs.
items.cn: administratio 指对事务的料理与管理。

items.en: Old French kept the word for the running of business and property.
items.cn: 古法语保留该词，指经营事务与财产。

items.en: English adopted administration for the conduct of public and private affairs.
items.cn: 英语采用 administration，指公共与私人事务的处理。

items.en: American usage made it a name for the government in office, while medicine kept the dosing sense.
items.cn: 美式用法使它成为「在任政府」的称呼，医学则保留了给药义。

note.en: The first group is the same Latin family; the second gathers words for management and governing bodies.
note.cn: 第一组同属一个拉丁词族；第二组收管理与治理机构方面的词。

entries.definition: the group that rules a country
an office that carries out public work

normalIntro.en: Take administer, add -ation, and you have the activity and the body that performs it.
normalIntro.cn: administer 加 -ation，就得到那项活动，也得到执行它的机构。

normal.en: The stem is minister, a servant, so administration began as service.
normal.cn: 词干是 minister（仆人），所以 administration 最初是「服务」。

normal.en: Business administration and public administration are two fixed degree names.
normal.cn: business administration 与 public administration 是两个固定的学位名称。

normal.en: In American news, the administration means the sitting government.
normal.cn: 在美国新闻里，the administration 指正在执政的政府。

normal.en: Drug administration is the medical phrase for giving a dose.
normal.cn: drug administration 是医学上「给药」的说法。

normal.en: The plural administrations covers several governments or several managing bodies.
normal.cn: 复数 administrations 指多届政府或多套管理班子。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of offices where every form must be stamped.
abstract.cn: 想象一条办公室走廊，每份表格都要盖章。

abstract.en: See a cabinet table where a whole government sits.
abstract.cn: 想象一张内阁会议桌，坐着一整届政府。

abstract.en: Think of a nurse's tray with the dose already measured.
abstract.cn: 想象护士的托盘，药量已经量好。

examples.en: She studied business administration in college.
examples.cn: 她在大学学的是工商管理。

examples.en: The administration rejected the proposal.
examples.cn: 政府否决了这项提案。

examples.en: The nurse recorded the administration of the drug.
examples.cn: 护士记录了这次给药。

root: 拉丁语 administratio（事务的料理），出自 administrare（服务、管理）与 minister（仆人）；本义「替人理事」，后指管理机构与政府。

sensesIntro.en: The act, the people and the government share one noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 行为、人群与政府，共用这一个名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: papers moving through a corridor of offices.
core.cn: 核心意象：文件在一层层办公室之间流转。

branches.en: the quiet work that keeps a school open
branches.cn: 让学校得以运转的幕后工作

branches.en: the staff who sign the forms
a government in its first year
a measured dose handed to a patient

latinIntro.cn: 其他由动词变来的 -tion 名词，也指活动而非施动者。

definition_zh: 行政的；管理的；（处罚）非刑事的
definition_en: relating to the management and organization of an institution, or to decisions made by officials rather than by courts
core_image: 办公桌上摊开一摞表格，每一栏都要签字盖章
scene: 报销单在三个窗口之间转了一圈，最后还是缺一个章。The delay was purely administrative, not a rejection.
sceneCN: 这里的 administrative 是「行政上的」（第 1 个义项：与管理工作有关）；句意是这次延误纯粹是行政手续问题，并非否决。

pos.zh: 形容词：行政的；管理的；行政性的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词词干还原为动词，义为「管理；施行」

由词干加表人后缀构成，义为「管理者」

senses.title: Relating to management work
senses.definition: connected with the organizing and running of an institution rather than its main activity
senses.definitionCN: 与机构的组织运转有关，而非与其主要业务直接有关
senses.example: She works as an administrative assistant in the dean's office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在院长办公室做行政助理。
senses.why: The suffix -ive turns the managing verb into a describing word: whatever belongs to the running of affairs is administrative.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ive 把「管理」这一动词变成形容词：凡属于事务运转的，就是 administrative。

senses.title: Decided by officials, not courts
senses.definition: describing penalties, decisions or law handled by public officials or agencies rather than by criminal courts
senses.definitionCN: 指由公共机关或官员而非刑事法庭处理的处罚、决定或法律
senses.example: The fine was an administrative penalty, not a criminal conviction.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔罚款是行政处罚，不是刑事定罪。
senses.why: Law divides the field: courts handle crimes, while the executive machinery handles its own affairs, and those belong to administrative law.
senses.whyCN: 法律把领域分开：法院处理犯罪，行政机关处理自身事务，后者归入行政法。

intro.en: A Latin adjective built on the verb of managing.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁形容词，建立在表示「管理」的动词之上。

items.en: ministrare meant to serve or supply, from minister, a servant.
items.cn: ministrare 意为服侍或供给，出自 minister（仆人）。

items.en: administrare meant to manage or carry on affairs.
items.cn: administrare 意为管理、经办事务。

items.en: administrativus was formed with -ivus, meaning serving to manage.
items.cn: administrativus 由 -ivus 构成，意为「用于管理的」。

items.en: English took administrative in the eighteenth century with the growth of modern offices and public bodies.
items.cn: 随着近代办公机构与公共机关的成长，英语在十八世纪采用 administrative。

items.en: It now covers office work, public law and penalties that never reach a criminal court.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖办公事务、公法，以及不会进入刑事法庭的处罚。

note.en: The first group shares the managing stem; the second gathers adjectives of office work and official control.
note.cn: 第一组共享「管理」词干；第二组收与办公事务、官方管理相关的形容词。

entries.definition: bound by official rules and paperwork

normal.en: administrative work is the paperwork that supports the main job.
normal.cn: administrative work 是支撑主要业务的那些文书工作。

normal.en: administrative law governs public bodies rather than private citizens.
normal.cn: administrative law（行政法）约束的是公共机构。

normal.en: administrative staff are the people who keep the forms moving.
normal.cn: administrative staff 是让表格流转起来的人。

senses.title: A person who manages an institution
senses.definition: someone whose job is to organize and run the affairs of an organization

senses.example: The hospital administrator approved the new rota.
senses.exampleCN: 医院管理者批准了新的排班表。
senses.why: Latin -or marks the person who performs the verb, so administrator is the one who carries on administrare, the managing of affairs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 -or 标记执行动词的人，所以 administrator 就是承担 administrare（管理事务）的那个人。

senses.title: A person appointed to settle an estate
senses.definition: a person legally appointed to manage and distribute the property of someone who has died
senses.definitionCN: 依法被指定管理并分配死者财产的人
senses.example: A court appointed an administrator to settle the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 法院指定了一名管理人来处理遗产。
senses.why: When no executor is named, the court needs someone to handle the property, and the general word for handling affairs is used.
senses.whyCN: 若遗嘱没有指定执行人，法院就需要有人来处理财产，于是用了这个表示「料理事务」的通用词。

senses.title: A person who runs a computer system

senses.example: Contact the network administrator if the printer goes offline.
senses.exampleCN: 如果打印机掉线，请联系网络管理员。
senses.why: Computing took over the old job title because a server, like an office, needs someone to keep its accounts and permissions in order.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用了这个旧职称，因为服务器和办公室一样，需要有人维护账号与权限。

definition_zh: 钦佩；赞赏；令人钦佩的对象
definition_en: a feeling of great respect and warm approval, or the person or thing that causes it
core_image: 人群抬头看着走钢丝的人抵达对面，忍不住鼓起掌来
scene: 演出结束，观众站起来鼓掌，久久不肯离场。Her courage won the admiration of everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里的 admiration 是「钦佩」（第 1 个义项：由衷的敬意）；句意是她的勇气赢得了在场所有人的钦佩。

pos.zh: 名词：钦佩；赞赏；令人钦佩的人或物

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「钦佩；欣赏」

由动词词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「值得钦佩的」
由动词加分词后缀构成，义为「赞赏的」

senses.title: A feeling of great respect
senses.definition: a feeling of respect mixed with warm approval for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物怀有的敬意，并带温暖的赞许
senses.example: She looked at the painting with admiration.
senses.exampleCN: 她怀着钦佩之情看着那幅画。
senses.why: Latin admirari joined ad- 'to' with mirari 'to wonder', so admiration is wonder turned towards something worth looking up to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 admirari 是 ad-（向）加 mirari（惊叹），所以 admiration 是「惊叹」转向某个值得仰望的对象。

senses.title: The person or thing admired
senses.definition: someone or something that is the object of widespread praise and wonder
senses.definitionCN: 广受赞美与惊叹的人或事物
senses.example: The young pianist was the admiration of the whole school.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻的钢琴手成了全校钦佩的对象。
senses.why: The feeling and its object exchange places easily: what everyone wonders at becomes, in the old phrase, the admiration of all.
senses.whyCN: 情感与对象很容易互换位置：众人惊叹之物，用旧说法就是「众人的 admiration」。

intro.en: Wonder, directed at something, becomes respect.
intro.cn: 惊叹一旦指向某个对象，就成了敬意。

items.en: mirari meant to wonder at or marvel, and gave mirror and miracle.
items.cn: mirari 意为惊叹、惊奇，也生出 mirror 与 miracle。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus mirari formed admirari, to wonder at, to regard with wonder.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 mirari 构成 admirari，意为「对……惊叹、以惊奇的目光看待」。

items.en: admiratio named the feeling of wonder and esteem.
items.cn: admiratio 指惊叹与敬意交织的情感。

items.en: Old French carried the noun into English with the sense of wondering esteem.
items.cn: 古法语把这个名词带入英语，义为「带着惊叹的敬重」。

items.en: The modern word is milder than wonder: it praises without losing distance.
items.cn: 现代词义比「惊叹」温和：它在赞美时仍保持一点距离。

note.en: The first group is the mirari family; the second gathers feelings of approval with different heat.
note.cn: 第一组是 mirari 词族；第二组收几种热度不同的赞许之情。

entries.definition: a feeling of esteem for someone

normal.en: admire plus -ation gives the feeling; admire plus -er gives the person who feels it.
normal.cn: admire 加 -ation 是情感，加 -er 是怀有情感的人。

normal.cn: 常用搭配是 admiration for（对……的钦佩）。

normal.cn: in admiration 描述一个人看或说的神态。

normal.en: admiration is uncountable in the feeling sense.
normal.cn: 表示「情感」时，admiration 不可数。

normal.en: Keep the -ation ending; do not write admirment.
normal.cn: 词尾是 -ation，不要写成 admirment。

definition_en: to respect someone or something greatly, or to look at something with pleasure

scene: 老人每天傍晚都站在海边，什么也不做，只是望着落日。She stood at the window and admired the sunset.
sceneCN: 这里的 admired 是「欣赏」（第 2 个义项：带着愉悦观看）；句意是她站在窗前欣赏落日。

senses.title: To respect someone greatly
senses.definition: to have a high opinion of someone because of their qualities or actions
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的品质或行为而对他评价很高
senses.example: I admire her for speaking out.
senses.exampleCN: 我钦佩她敢于直言。
senses.why: Latin admirari is to wonder at, and wonder aimed at a person's conduct settles into steady respect.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 admirari 是「对……惊叹」，当惊叹对准一个人的行为，就沉淀为稳定的敬重。

senses.title: To look at something with pleasure
senses.definition: to enjoy looking at something beautiful or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 愉悦地观看美丽或令人印象深刻的事物
senses.example: We stopped on the bridge to admire the view.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在桥上停下来欣赏景色。
senses.why: The same wondering gaze can rest on a view rather than a person, and then the verb means to enjoy looking.
senses.whyCN: 同样那种惊叹的目光也可以落在风景而非人身上，这时动词就表示「愉悦地看」。

senses.title: To praise openly
senses.definition: to express approval of someone or something in words
senses.definitionCN: 用言语对某人或某物表示赞许
senses.example: The teacher admired his careful handwriting.
senses.exampleCN: 老师称赞他字写得仔细。
senses.why: Respect that is spoken aloud becomes praise, so the verb can simply mean to say good things about something.
senses.whyCN: 敬重一旦说出口就成了赞美，所以这个动词也可以只表示「说好话」。

intro.en: To wonder at something is the oldest sense of the verb.
intro.cn: 「对某物感到惊叹」是这个动词最古老的意思。

items.en: mirari meant to wonder or marvel at something.
items.cn: mirari 意为对某物感到惊奇、赞叹。

items.cn: ad-（向）加 mirari 构成 admirari，意为「以惊叹与敬重看待」。

items.en: Old French admirer kept both the wondering and the esteeming senses.
items.cn: 古法语 admirer 同时保留惊叹与敬重两层意思。

items.en: English adopted admire in the sixteenth century, often for looking at something with delight.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪采用 admire，常指愉悦地观看某物。

items.en: Today the verb covers respect for people, pleasure in views and spoken praise.
items.cn: 今天这个动词涵盖对人的敬重、对景色的欣赏与口头的赞美。

senses.title: The right to enter a place
senses.definition: permission or the right to enter a building, event or institution
senses.definitionCN: 进入某座建筑、活动或机构的许可或权利
senses.example: Admission is by ticket only.
senses.exampleCN: 只有凭票才能入场。
senses.why: Latin admissio came from admittere, to let in, so the noun first means the door being opened for you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 admissio 出自 admittere（放进来），所以这个名词首先指「门为你打开」这件事。

senses.title: The price paid to enter
senses.definition: the money charged for entering a place such as a museum or a show
senses.definitionCN: 进入博物馆、演出等场所所需支付的费用
senses.example: The museum charges a small admission fee.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆收取少量入场费。
senses.why: The right to enter became a thing sold, and the abstract permission turned into a concrete charge.
senses.whyCN: 进入的权利变成了可以出售的东西，抽象的许可于是转成具体的收费。

senses.title: A statement that something is true
senses.definition: a statement in which someone accepts that something unpleasant or damaging is true
senses.definitionCN: 某人接受某件不愉快或不利之事为真的陈述
senses.example: His admission of guilt surprised the court.
senses.exampleCN: 他认罪让法庭感到意外。
senses.why: To admit is also to let a fact in, past the resistance that kept it outside.
senses.whyCN: admit 也有「让一个事实进来」之义，越过先前把它挡在外面的那道阻力。

senses.title: Acceptance into a group or hospital
senses.definition: the act of accepting someone as a member, a student or a patient
senses.definitionCN: 接受某人成为成员、学生或病人的行为
senses.example: The school has tightened its admission policy.
senses.exampleCN: 学校收紧了招生政策。
senses.why: Institutions also open their doors: the same letting-in names entry to a school or a ward.
senses.whyCN: 机构同样会「开门」：同一个「放进来」也指进入学校或病房。

intro.cn: 「被放进来」的名词，出自一个表示「向……送去」的拉丁动词。

items.en: admissio named the act of letting someone in.

items.en: English borrowed admission for entry to a place, and soon for accepting a fact.
items.cn: 英语借入 admission 表示进入某地，很快也指接受某个事实。

items.en: Schools and hospitals made it a fixed term for accepting students and patients.
items.cn: 学校与医院使它成为「录取学生、收治病人」的固定用语。

note.en: The first group is the admit family; the second gathers words for entry, payment and confession.
note.cn: 第一组是 admit 词族；第二组收进入、费用与坦白三路词。

definition_zh: 承认；准许进入；接纳；容纳

core_image: 门卫侧身让开一步，抬手示意你进去
scene: 证据摆在桌上，他沉默了很久，终于低下头。He finally admitted that he had taken the money.
sceneCN: 这里的 admitted 是「承认」（第 1 个义项：不情愿地认可某事为真）；句意是他终于承认自己拿了那笔钱。

senses.title: To agree that something is true
senses.definition: to accept that something is true, often with reluctance or against one's interest
senses.definitionCN: 接受某事为真，常带不情愿或违背自身利益
senses.example: He admitted to breaking the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认打碎了窗户。
senses.why: Latin admittere meant to let in: a fact is let past the resistance that kept it out, which is why the verb often feels unwilling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 admittere 意为「放进来」：一个事实被放过了先前挡住它的那道阻力，所以这个动词常带不情愿的味道。

senses.title: To allow someone to enter
senses.definition: to allow a person to enter a place, especially after checking
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人进入某处，尤指经查验之后
senses.example: Only ticket holders will be admitted.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持票者才被允许入场。
senses.why: This is the plainest sense: the door is opened and the person is let through.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的一层：门被打开，人被放过。

senses.title: To take someone into a hospital or school
senses.definition: to accept someone as a patient in a hospital or as a student in a school
senses.definitionCN: 接收某人为医院病人或学校学生
senses.example: She was admitted to hospital with chest pain.
senses.exampleCN: 她因胸痛被收治入院。
senses.why: Institutions repeat the gate-keeping gesture: a patient or a student is allowed inside the system.
senses.whyCN: 机构重复了「守门放行」的动作：病人或学生被允许进入这套系统。

senses.title: To have room for
senses.definition: to provide enough space for a number of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 为一定数量的人或物提供足够的空间
senses.example: The hall admits five hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅能容纳五百人。
senses.why: A place that admits lets things into itself, so capacity itself can be expressed with the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 一个「放进来」的场所是把东西收进自身，所以容纳量也能用同一个动词表达。

intro.en: A verb of letting in, which also lets in facts.
intro.cn: 一个「放进来」的动词，也把事实放进来。

items.en: mittere meant to send or let go.
items.cn: mittere 意为送出、放行。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus mittere formed admittere, to let in or allow to approach.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「放进来、允许靠近」。

items.en: The participle admissus described someone who had been let in.
items.cn: 分词 admissus 描述「已被放进来」的人。

items.en: English used admit for entry to a place, then for accepting an opinion.
items.cn: 英语先用 admit 表示进入某地，后用来表示接受某种看法。

items.en: Hospitals and schools fixed the passive be admitted to, and the verb also came to mean to hold a capacity.
items.cn: 医院与学校固定了被动式 be admitted to，这个词也引申出「容纳」之义。

note.en: The first group is the admit family; the second gathers verbs of confessing, allowing and holding.
note.cn: 第一组是 admit 词族；第二组收承认、允许与容纳三类动词。

definition_zh: 青少年；青春期的；不成熟的
definition_en: a young person between childhood and adulthood, or relating to that stage of life
core_image: 一个正在长个子的少年，袖子短了一截，声音也变低了
scene: 他一年长了十厘米，鞋码换了两次，说话却还是吞吞吐吐。The adolescent boy stood awkwardly at the door.
sceneCN: 这里的 adolescent 是「青春期的」（第 2 个义项：属于少年阶段的）；句意是那个青春期的男孩局促地站在门口。

pos.zh: 名词：青少年
形容词：青春期的；不成熟的

derivatives.zh: 由词干加名词后缀构成，义为「青春期；少年时代」

senses.title: A young person growing up
senses.definition: a person who is no longer a child but not yet an adult
senses.definitionCN: 已经不再是儿童、但尚未成为成年人的人
senses.example: Many adolescents struggle with lack of sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 许多青少年饱受睡眠不足之苦。
senses.why: Latin adolescere means to grow up, and its participle names the one who is in the middle of that growing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adolescere 意为「长大」，它的分词就指正处在这一成长过程中的人。

senses.title: Relating to the teenage stage
senses.definition: connected with the period of life between childhood and adulthood
senses.definitionCN: 与童年与成年之间那个人生阶段有关的
senses.example: The clinic offers advice to adolescent patients.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为青少年病人提供建议。
senses.why: The same participle also works as an adjective, describing anything that belongs to that stretch of growing up.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词也能作形容词，描述属于那段成长时期的一切。

senses.title: Immature in manner
senses.definition: behaving in a way that seems immature for one's age
senses.definitionCN: 行为方式相对于年龄显得不够成熟
senses.example: His adolescent humour annoyed the older staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他那套幼稚的幽默让年长的同事很烦。
senses.why: Because the stage is halfway to adulthood, the adjective can be used to criticise behaviour that has not finished growing.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个阶段只走到成年的一半，形容词便可用来批评尚未「长成」的行为。

intro.en: The word names a person in the middle of growing up.
intro.cn: 这个词指一个正处在成长中途的人。

items.en: alescere was an inchoative verb meaning to begin to grow.
items.cn: alescere 是表示「开始生长」的起始动词。

items.en: ad- plus alescere formed adolescere, to grow up, to come to maturity.
items.cn: ad- 加 alescere 构成 adolescere，意为「长大、成熟起来」。

items.en: The present participle adolescens named a young person still growing.
items.cn: 现在分词 adolescens 指仍在成长的年轻人。

items.en: French passed the adjective and noun into English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 法语在十五世纪把这个形容词与名词一并传入英语。

items.en: Medicine and psychology gave the word a precise age range and a set of typical problems.
items.cn: 医学与心理学给这个词划定了大致年龄范围，并附上一组典型问题。

note.en: The first group shares the growing root; the second gathers words for young people.
note.cn: 第一组共享「生长」词根；第二组收指年轻人的词。

normal.en: The noun for the stage is adolescence, with -ence instead of -ent.

normal.en: The word can be a noun or an adjective without changing form.

abstract.en: Think of shoes bought twice in one year.
abstract.cn: 想象一年里买了两次鞋。

examples.en: Adolescent behaviour can be hard for parents to read.
examples.cn: 青少年的行为有时让父母难以理解。

definition_en: to take a child into your family legally, to start using a method or idea, or to formally approve a proposal
core_image: 会议桌上有人举起一份文件，众人跟着举手
scene: 公司试了新流程半年，效果不错，于是各部门都开始照着做。The committee adopted the new safety rules unanimously.
sceneCN: 这里的 adopted 是「正式通过」（第 3 个义项：经表决批准）；句意是委员会一致通过了新的安全规定。

senses.title: To take a child into a family legally
senses.definition: to take another person's child into your family and become its legal parent
senses.definitionCN: 把他人的孩子接入自己家庭，并成为其法定父母
senses.example: They adopted a girl from the same town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们收养了同镇的一个女孩。
senses.why: Latin adoptare is ad- 'to' plus optare 'to choose', so adoption is literally choosing a child as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adoptare 是 ad-（向）加 optare（选择），所以收养字面上就是「选择一人作为自己的孩子」。

senses.title: To start using a method or idea
senses.definition: to begin to use a particular method, attitude or style
senses.definitionCN: 开始使用某种方法、态度或风格
senses.example: The school adopted a new teaching method.
senses.exampleCN: 学校采用了一种新的教学法。
senses.why: If a child can be chosen into a family, a method can be chosen into practice; the same act of taking something as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 孩子可以被选进家庭，方法也可以被选进实践；都是「把某物认作自己的」这同一个动作。

senses.title: To formally approve a proposal
senses.definition: to accept and approve a formal proposal, report or set of rules by vote
senses.definitionCN: 经表决接受并批准正式提案、报告或规则
senses.example: Parliament adopted the budget after a long debate.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长时间辩论，议会通过了预算。
senses.why: A committee takes a text as its own by voting, and the word for taking something as one's own covers that act too.
senses.whyCN: 委员会通过表决把一份文本认作自己的，而「认作己有」这个词正好涵盖这一动作。

intro.en: At the root is a verb of choosing.
intro.cn: 词根处是一个表示「选择」的动词。

items.en: optare meant to choose or wish, and it also gives option and opt.
items.cn: optare 意为选择、希望，也生出 option 与 opt。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus optare formed adoptare, to take as one's own by choice.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 optare 构成 adoptare，意为「选来作为自己的」。

items.en: adoptio was the legal act of taking a child as one's own.

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转作形容词，义为「先进的；高级的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「推进；提升」

senses.title: To move forward
senses.definition: to move forward in space, especially as a group or force
senses.definitionCN: 在空间中向前移动，尤指成群或成队地
senses.example: The army advanced through the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 部队穿过山谷向前推进。
senses.why: Old French avancer came from Latin abante, from before, so the word pictures something coming forward from where it was.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 avancer 出自拉丁语 abante（从前面），这个词画出的是某物从原处向前出来的动作。

senses.title: Progress or improvement
senses.definition: a development or improvement in knowledge, technology or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 知识、技术或局势上的发展或改善
senses.example: Medical science has advanced rapidly.
senses.exampleCN: 医学发展得很快。
senses.why: Moving forward in space became moving forward in time and quality, so any step ahead counts as an advance.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的前移变成时间与质量上的前移，于是任何向前的一步都算一次 advance。

senses.title: Before the expected time
senses.definition: before a particular time or date, especially in the phrase in advance
senses.definitionCN: 在某个时间或日期之前，尤用于短语 in advance
senses.example: Please book your tickets in advance.
senses.exampleCN: 请提前订票。
senses.why: What is in advance is placed ahead of the event, the same forward image applied to time.
senses.whyCN: in advance 的东西被放在事件之前，正是同一个「向前」的画面用在时间上。

senses.title: Money paid ahead of time
senses.definition: money given before it is due, or as a loan or first instalment
senses.definitionCN: 在应付之前给出的钱，或作为借款、首期款
senses.example: The publisher gave her an advance on the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社为这部小说预付了她一笔钱。
senses.why: Payment can also be moved earlier, and the noun names the money that arrives before the work does.
senses.whyCN: 付款同样可以被提前，名词便指那笔先于成果到达的钱。

senses.title: To put forward an idea
senses.definition: to suggest or present an idea, theory or claim for consideration
senses.definitionCN: 提出某个想法、理论或主张供人考虑
senses.example: She advanced a bold theory about the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 她提出了一个关于这种疾病的大胆理论。
senses.why: To advance a proposal is to bring it forward into view, the same motion from behind to the front.
senses.whyCN: 提出一项主张，就是把它从后面推到人前，还是同一个由后向前的动作。

intro.en: A word built on the Latin phrase from before.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语「从前面」这一说法上。

items.en: abante meant from before or in front, from ab 'from' plus ante 'before'.
items.cn: abante 意为「从前面」，由 ab（从）与 ante（前）构成。

items.en: Late Latin and Vulgar Latin reshaped the phrase into a verb of moving forward.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语与通俗拉丁语把这一说法改造成表示「前移」的动词。

items.en: avancer meant to move forward, to promote, and to lend money ahead of time.
items.cn: avancer 意为前移、提升，也指提前借钱给人。

items.en: English took the verb in the thirteenth century and the noun soon after.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入动词，名词紧随其后。

items.en: Finance kept the sense of money paid early, while science and warfare kept the sense of moving ahead.
items.cn: 金融保留了「提前付钱」之义，科学与军事则保留了「向前推进」之义。

note.en: The first group shares the forward root; the second gathers words for moving and improving.
note.cn: 第一组共享「向前」词根；第二组收前进与提升两路词。

normalIntro.en: The core picture is something placed in front.
normalIntro.cn: 核心画面是把某物放到前面。

normal.en: in advance is the phrase to learn first; it covers time and money.
normal.cn: 先记住 in advance，它同时管时间与钱。

normal.en: advance payment and advance notice both put something before its due moment.
normal.cn: advance payment 与 advance notice 都是把事提前。

normal.en: advanced is the adjective, advancement the noun of process.
normal.cn: advanced 是形容词，advancement 是表示过程的名词。

normal.en: The past tense is advanced, with a single t after the c.
normal.cn: 过去式是 advanced，c 后面只有一个 t。

normal.en: Do not mix it up with advantage, which means a benefit.
normal.cn: 别与 advantage 混淆，后者意为「优势」。

abstract.cn: 想象旗帜先于士兵出现在山脊上。

abstract.en: Picture a train leaving the platform a minute early.
abstract.cn: 想象列车提前一分钟离站。

abstract.en: Think of money handed over before the work begins.
abstract.cn: 想象在工作开始前先递过去一笔钱。

definition_zh: 优势；有利条件；利益；（网球）占先
definition_en: something that puts you in a better position, or a benefit gained from a situation
core_image: 两个人赛跑，一个站在下坡，一个站在上坡
scene: 同样的价格，这家店出门就是地铁，那家要转两趟车。Living near the station is a real advantage.
sceneCN: 这里的 advantage 是「有利条件」（第 1 个义项：使人处于更有利位置的因素）；句意是住在车站附近是个实实在在的优势。

pos.zh: 名词：优势；有利条件；利益；（网球）占先

derivatives.zh: 加否定前缀 dis- 构成，义为「不利条件；劣势」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「有利的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「有利地」
由名词加分词后缀构成，义为「处于有利地位的」

senses.title: A condition that puts you ahead
senses.definition: a circumstance or quality that gives someone a better chance than others
senses.definitionCN: 使某人比他人更有机会的处境或特质
senses.example: Her fluent Spanish gave her an advantage in the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她流利的西班牙语让她在面试中占了优势。
senses.why: Old French avantage came from avant, before: an advantage is a position slightly ahead of the others.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 avantage 出自 avant（在前）：优势就是比他人稍稍靠前的位置。

senses.title: A benefit gained
senses.definition: a useful or favourable result that comes from something
senses.definitionCN: 由某事带来的有用或有利的结果
senses.example: We should take advantage of the fine weather.
senses.exampleCN: 我们应该利用这段好天气。
senses.why: Being ahead is useful, and the word slides from the lead itself to the gain it brings.
senses.whyCN: 领先本身有用，于是词义从「领先的位置」滑到「由此得到的好处」。

senses.title: The point after deuce in tennis
senses.definition: the first point won after deuce, which puts a player one point from the game
senses.definitionCN: 平局后赢下的第一分，使球员距赢下该局只差一分
senses.example: The player held advantage after the long rally.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间多拍回合之后，这名球员保持着占先。
senses.why: Tennis uses the old idea of being ahead: after deuce, one player stands one point in front.
senses.whyCN: 网球沿用「领先」这一旧义：平局之后，一方只比别人多出一分。

intro.en: The noun of being in front, from Latin before.
intro.cn: 一个表示「在前」的名词，出自拉丁语的「前」。

items.en: ante meant before or in front of.
items.cn: ante 意为在……之前、在……前面。

items.en: abante, from before, gave the French words for moving ahead.
items.cn: abante（从前面）生出法语中表示前移的词。

items.en: avant meant before or in front, and avantage meant a place in front.
items.cn: avant 意为在前，avantage 指「靠前的位置」。

items.en: English adopted advantage for a favourable position in a contest.
items.cn: 英语借入 advantage，指竞争中有利的位置。

items.en: Business added competitive advantage, and tennis gave the word a fixed scoring sense.
items.cn: 商业添上 competitive advantage，网球则给它一个固定的计分义。

note.en: The first group is the avant family; the second gathers words for a lead and for benefit.
note.cn: 第一组是 avant 词族；第二组收领先与好处两类词。

normal.en: take advantage of is the phrase that appears most often in exams.
normal.cn: take advantage of 是考试里出现最多的搭配。

normal.en: advantage over is used when two sides are compared.

definition_zh: 冒险；奇遇；冒险精神；大胆的尝试
definition_en: an unusual and exciting experience, the willingness to take risks, or a bold new enterprise
core_image: 一张摊开的地图，边角画着还没走过的海岸线
scene: 他们辞了工作，开着一辆旧车往西走，没有计划。Their trip across the desert turned into a real adventure.
sceneCN: 这里的 adventure 是「冒险经历」（第 1 个义项：不寻常而刺激的经历）；句意是他们穿越沙漠的旅行变成了一场真正的冒险。

pos.zh: 名词：冒险；奇遇；冒险精神；大胆尝试

derivatives.zh: 由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「爱冒险的；惊险的」
由名词加表人后缀构成，义为「冒险家」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「爱冒险地」
加前缀 mis- 构成，义为「不幸的遭遇；意外事故」

senses.title: An exciting and unusual experience
senses.definition: an unusual, exciting and possibly risky experience or journey
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常、令人兴奋且可能带风险的经历或旅程
senses.example: The climb was the adventure of a lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 那次攀登是一生只有一次的冒险。
senses.why: Latin adventurus means about to happen, from advenire, to come to; an adventure is whatever is coming towards you, unknown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adventurus 意为「即将发生」，出自 advenire（来临）；adventure 就是那件正朝你走来、尚不可知的事。

senses.title: A willingness to take risks
senses.definition: the quality of being eager to try new or risky things
senses.definitionCN: 乐于尝试新鲜或冒险之事的性格
senses.example: She has a real sense of adventure.
senses.exampleCN: 她真有冒险精神。
senses.why: The events gave their name to the appetite for them, so the noun can mean the spirit rather than the trip.
senses.whyCN: 这类事件把自己的名字给了对它的渴望，于是名词可以指精神而非旅程。

senses.title: A bold and risky enterprise
senses.definition: a new project or business venture that involves considerable risk
senses.definitionCN: 涉及相当风险的新项目或商业尝试
senses.example: Starting the company was a costly adventure.
senses.exampleCN: 创办这家公司是一次代价高昂的冒险。
senses.why: Business likes the word for its hint of the unknown: a new firm is a journey with no map.
senses.whyCN: 商业喜欢这个词所带的「未知」意味：一家新公司就是一次没有地图的旅程。

intro.en: What is about to happen, and therefore uncertain.
intro.cn: 「即将发生之事」，因而也是不确定之事。

items.en: venire meant to come, and underlies invent, prevent and convene.
items.cn: venire 意为来，invent、prevent 与 convene 都出自它。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus venire formed advenire, to come to, to arrive.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 venire 构成 advenire，意为「来到、抵达」。

items.en: adventura meant the things that are about to happen, often used of chance or fate.
items.cn: adventura 指「即将发生的事」，常用于机遇或命运。

items.en: Old French aventure named a knight's chance encounter and the tale told about it.
items.cn: 古法语 aventure 指骑士的偶然遭遇，以及围绕它讲的故事。

items.en: English adopted adventure for risky journeys, then for the spirit that seeks them.
items.cn: 英语借入 adventure 指有风险的旅程，后又指追寻它的那股精神。

note.en: The first group is the coming root; the second gathers words for risky journeys and ventures.
note.cn: 第一组是表示「来」的词根；第二组收有风险的旅程与事业。
